observation: Two census agents before the interview turned a seven-line plan into facts the founder could rule on: nobody could stop a session, the viewer had no door, the key was written to a table nothing read, the composition root joined routers but not action lists. Four rulings in four questions, one at a time, each with a recommendation and the impact stated in plain words when asked ('what's the impact of that?').

The critique of the architecture note blocked on two things the note asserted and the builders would have shipped: teardown could only write done/crashed, so a stop would have read as completed and auto-finished the task; and the governance rule cannot be green between declaring an action and wiring its screen. Both became decisions before any code.
evidence: critique 1 (B1, B2); D-njr2es, D-9p94bz; architecture.md section 12

observation: The first fix for the stop flag set it inside the registry's abort callback, which opencode's own clean return also reaches; the test that certified it fired the return before the session was registered, so it passed for the wrong reason. The reviewer traced the call chain and the test's timing; the second fix moved the discriminator to the call site (abort reason 'stop' | 'return') and the test fires the return from the adapter stream after registration, with a revert-and-watch-red proof.

Two builders sharing one worktree each once ran a bare `git commit` after `git add <own files>` and swept the other builder's staged deletions into their commit; both caught it with `git show --stat HEAD` and undid it with `git reset --soft`. The preamble now requires the pathspec on the commit itself (`git commit -m ... -- <files>`).
evidence: T-7gy3zv and T-9v5m2t builder reports; scratchpad/bc6/preamble.md

observation: Builders cited decision ids, item ids and 'architecture.md §N' in plain comments and test titles across ~60 files despite the preamble rule; the sweep cost a dedicated fix task. The rule was worded 'never in code' — builders read comments and test titles as not code. The preamble now names comments, test titles and section references explicitly and asks for the constraint in words inside @lore.

Each deleting task missed at least one consumer that grep by import could not find: a test that hit the deleted route over HTTP (P3-credentials), a test that stubbed the deleted count route by URL (RecipientPicker), a vitest project entry for the deleted package, dependency rows knip flags. Only running the suite surfaced them. Consumer lists derived by import grep undercount; the builder brief should say 'run the neighbouring suites' rather than 'grep the imports'.

The packaged app walk proved what no lane could: a live claude session stopped from the new action — the harness process died, the row read stopped/stopped, the task stayed in progress; the viewer opened from both doors and went quiet on the nudge; the roster and the task page read the new list; a plugin installed through edit_plugin appeared on the page and was disabled from it; zero errors in the log.

The viewer's new Stop button landed under the split pane's floating expand/close icons on both doors — a placement defect no component test sees because the split's controls belong to another component. Found only by looking at the painted window.

The founder accepted deleting the server-side key on the condition that workers still work. The field exists and its keychain write is proven by tests, but the field only shows in shared-backend mode, no shared backend exists, and the worker's actual connect was not run. The plan said 'the worker connects for the first time'; the run could show the keychain path, not the connection. Reported as a limit, not claimed.
evidence: SettingsWorker.tsx shared-mode branch; walk: Backend section in local mode says worker mode is shared-only

observation: The architecture predicted ~1,555 added lines with ~520 relocated; the branch measures (whitespace-insensitive, production only) +2,991/−3,819 with 862 (plugin lifecycle) + 169 (cipher) relocated — roughly 1,960 new against the 1,000-new bar the founder accepted. The declarations alone are 392 lines (predicted 320), the two page splits and the viewer rewrite ~300, the websocket fold +322. The estimate was made from the route file sizes, not from the copies the pattern needs (orchestration's own action mirror and loops, a second page split).

The record has no checks or review configured for this project (idle doctor: checks [], review false), so every submitted task went straight to done on the builder's word; verification and review had to be run by the planner as extra agents. A wrong `checks` key is silent.

One interview (four rulings, two amendments), one architecture note with one critique (BLOCKED, two real), 12 planned tasks + 1 discovered (AH5 lane) + 3 fix waves + 1 UI placement fix, 2 independent review passes (FAIL, FAIL on a carried finding, then re-verify), 1 seam test, full verify + test:full (5,047) + service integration (1,752), one packaged desktop build and one manual walk. About a quarter of the builder effort was rework: the stop-flag fix twice, the id sweep, missed test consumers, knip rows. Result: 40 commits, production +2,991/−3,819 whitespace-insensitive, net −828.
